name: ed138
label: 2026 ED138
discovered: 2026-10-13 by Matthew Holman (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian) in the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's images of March to July 2026, with earlier images back to 2016-02-25; announced by the Minor Planet Center on 2026-10-27
sizeNote: About 1,000 km across, estimated from its brightness (Mario Juric); unmeasured. Albedo, rotation and pole unknown.

orbit.elements: JPL Small-Body Database, orbit solution 1 (2026-10-27, 74 observations 2016-02-25 to 2026-07-11, DE441/SB441-N16), osculating heliocentric elements at the epoch (ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api?sstr=2026%20ED138)
orbit.notes: Ecliptic and equinox of J2000; epoch JD 2461200.5 TDB (2026-06-09); argument of pericentre and mean anomaly at the epoch, no precession of the apsides or node. Two-body motion from one epoch: fine for decades at 43 au.
